summary_responses.response: Cloud microservices often suffer temporary overload and miscoordination, where standard retries fail to protect high-value transactions and instead amplify load through damaging retry storms. The paper proposes DiffTry, a simple, stateless, distributed mechanism that assigns priority-class-specific retry limits—giving high-priority requests more attempts—to protect valuable traffic without requiring overload sensors or inter-service coordination. The authors develop analytical models for tandem services using fluid and queueing approximations, then generalize them to arbitrary networks via an open flow model with iterative solutions that compute per-class rejection and end-to-end completion rates. They prove network-wide monotonicity and uniqueness conditions—guaranteed for DAG networks—demonstrating that DiffTry substantially lowers high-priority rejections while suppressing low-priority retry amplification. Simulations and a live Kubernetes service-mesh deployment confirm the predictions match measured rejection closely, boosting high-priority success to about 85% of completions as a drop-in plugin requiring no application changes.

summary_responses.response: The FAA has adopted a new airworthiness directive for certain Bombardier Model BD-700-2A12 airplanes following reports of low clearance in the right wing between fuel line couplings, hydraulic lines, harness brackets, and fuel vent tubes. summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management is issuing a direct final rule amending its Family and Medical Leave Act regulations in 5 CFR part 630 to incorporate statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case affected provisions may be withdrawn and replaced with a proposed rule. The 2021 changes make virtually all Federal civilian service—including temporary or intermittent positions—count toward the 12-month service requirement for FMLA and paid parental leave eligibility, clarify that annual and sick leave earned outside title 5 may substitute for unpaid FMLA leave, and exclude all Veterans Health Administration employees covered by 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage. The December 2023 amendment further allows honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to qualify toward that same 12-month eligibility requirement. Because paid parental leave substitutes for unpaid FMLA leave, these updates also affect eligibility for that benefit.
